indicators.note: the tips of a phrase are its two ends, so only the very first and very last letters are kept
after sends the piece named before it to the second position, behind the other

blocks.note: the two end letters of sure-fire
a wage is pay for work

explanation.surface: A complaint that money is thrown away on supposedly certain bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the pay behind the tips, so the tips lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is the waste matter carried off in drains and sewers.

clue.text: Bread is hot when left inside

indicators.note: something put inside sits within the other word, splitting it

blocks.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A baker's note that the loaf is still warm when the remainder is kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: STOLEN takes L into its middle: STOL-L-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas, a kind of sweet bread.

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it, and also puts it at the front

blocks.note: the first letter of western
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: The leading female star of country and western music, its first lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' does double work: it takes the opening letter of western and sets it at the front, before the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite word for a woman, an adult female.

clue.text: Old timer visiting hotel every year

blocks.note: a Grand is a common name for a large hotel, as in the Grand Hotel
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: An elderly regular who stays at the same hotel annually.
explanation.walkthrough: PA, per annum, is a common abbreviation on price lists and salaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a fond example of an old-timer, an elderly man.

blocks.note: first meaning: criticises harshly, as a reviewer does
second meaning: flat grey stones used for roofing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an inspector rejecting shoddy materials; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate is British for to criticise severely, and slates are thin rock tiles laid on roofs.

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so a word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a leader directs a band or orchestra

explanation.surface: A conductor's concert is aired on the radio, featuring songs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the leader is the principal violinist, but a band leader conducts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs for voice and piano, as by Schubert.

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put things in a new order, so the following letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap one's components into a new order.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the instruction: shuffle the letters of the two words and they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose is to change the order or position of things, swapping them around.

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family doctor forbids a showy, lavish event.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish bout of spending or a showy effort meant to impress.

blocks.note: surface reading: the best-selling dishes on a restaurant menu
setter's reading: busy routes across the main, the old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main courses' sounds like dinner, but the main is the ocean and courses are routes steered across it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the regular sea routes followed by merchant vessels, well used and so popular.

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
a low is the sound a cow makes

explanation.surface: A pupil is threatened with a poor mark coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like a poor grade but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To loom is to appear in a menacing way, as trouble or a deadline threatens.

clue.text: It can be realised with each viable alternative

definitions.note: a phrase for something that is possible; the answer is the adjective describing it

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so the letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A plan becomes possible when every workable option is considered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achievable is within reach, able to be accomplished or brought about.

clue.text: Shaved man first wins back a record

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: a, plus LP, a long-playing record
Ned is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A clean-shaven athlete is the first to reclaim a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed A LP leads and the man's name ends the word; the clue's 'man first' order is loose, as the record comes back to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To plane wood is to shave thin layers off its surface with a blade.

blocks.note: a plea is an earnest request, like a prayer
bound as in certain: it is bound to happen

explanation.surface: Prayer is certain to bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment and contentment, a near synonym for happiness.

clue.text: Satan destroyed a whole continent for her

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters before it fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: The devil laid waste to an entire continent on a woman's account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' is a deliberately vague definition: any woman's name fits, and the wordplay picks which.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia is a female first name, borne by the youngest daughter of the last Russian tsar.

blocks.note: surface reading: a person from the west of Italy
setter's reading: the word that makes a cowboy film an Italian-made western, which is itself Italian food

explanation.walkthrough: Cowboy films made in Italy in the 1960s were nicknamed after a pasta, so the pasta is the Italian a western can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is an Italian pasta, and it names the Italian-made cowboy film genre.

indicators.note: in places one item within the other, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A geometric shape found operating inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a three-dimensional shape tapering from a circular base to a point.

indicators.note: back signals the word should be taken in the opposite direction, read right to left

blocks.note: the first half of this word, kick, is a sharp flavour; its second half is the signal to turn it round

explanation.surface: A parasite needs a payoff, a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kickback' looks like one word meaning a bribe, but it splits into kick and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small biting fly; some females feed on blood.

indicators.note: in places one item within another, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to stick is to glue
cos is a type of long-leaved lettuce

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to put salad leaves into sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos is what Americans call romaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar and the body's main fuel.

blocks.note: surface reading: grip the slings or prams used to carry infants
setter's reading: a clutch is a set of laid eggs, and their casings carry chicks before hatching

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' reads as a verb, to grip, but is the noun for a nest of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The shells of a clutch of eggs hold the unborn chicks, so they carry the babies.

indicators.note: to include is to contain, so the answer is held within the run of words

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: Most lectures on art contain a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock, to surprise them.

blocks.note: first meaning: an official document giving permission
second meaning: excessive freedom, disregard of moral restraint

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb phrase, 'Permit debauchery' sounds like allowing an orgy; both words are nouns here. British spelling uses -ence for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is an official permit, and licence also means unrestrained, immoral behaviour.

blocks.note: surface reading: a place where you rise to set off, or to confront someone
setter's reading: a fixture where men stand to relieve themselves, 'go' being the euphemism

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the polite word for using the toilet, and the fixture is the one used standing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wall-mounted toilet fixture used by men while standing.

clue.text: Europeans hop off westbound air transport

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are jumbled
in an across entry west is leftward, so travelling west means reading right to left

blocks.note: the European Union
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continental travellers fly west by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air transport' reads as one phrase, but transport is the definition, in the sense of being carried away by emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A transport of joy is an overwhelming feeling of delight, which is euphoria.

clue.text: Heckle when head removed from drink

indicators.note: removing the head takes away the front, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker or player

explanation.surface: Jeering at someone after a head was knocked off a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrack is a strong spirit distilled in South and Southeast Asia from palm sap or rice.

clue.text: Destroy tug, it's said, with part of leaf

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the words count by how they are pronounced

blocks.note: to wreck is to destroy
to tow is to pull, to tug

explanation.surface: Sabotaging a tugboat along with some foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: A leaf here is a page of a book, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page, the front side of a leaf in a book.

blocks.note: first meaning: happening by chance, dependent on something uncertain
second meaning: a group of troops sent to join a larger force

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at friendly fire; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingent as an adjective means occurring by chance; as a noun it is a detachment of troops.

blocks.note: C is a musical key
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: The specialist language of essential workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key workers' reads as a set phrase for essential staff, but splits into a musical key and the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is the special vocabulary of a particular group, a kind of jargon.

clue.text: Harmless drug given to short French vicar

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Dawn French played the Vicar of Dibley in the BBC sitcom

explanation.surface: A mild narcotic is handed to a French clergyman who is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' is not the nationality: The Vicar of Dibley is a British TV comedy starring Dawn French as the village vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edible is safe to eat, so harmless when eaten.

blocks.note: first meaning: turn into, grow to be
second meaning: look good on, flatter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests getting dressed in a suit; 'suit' is a verb here, as in 'that colour suits you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To become is to turn into something, and a garment that becomes you flatters you.
